name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,558

clue.text: Buttonhole with a carnation initially added to price

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the flower named just before it
added to says the earlier pieces are attached in front of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of carnation
the price of something is what it costs

explanation.surface: A man wearing a carnation buttonhole, with its cost added on to the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Buttonhole looks like a noun for the flower in a lapel, but here it is a verb: to buttonhole someone is to stop them and talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole a person is to approach and detain them in conversation, which is exactly what accosting someone means.

clue.text: Last word written by Dickens' first editor corrected

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the novelist's name

blocks.note: the word that closes a prayer
the opening letter of Dickens
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A literary anecdote about the final word Dickens wrote and the editor who fixed it.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been amended has had changes made to put errors right, so it has been corrected.

clue.text: Hide money for the audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

blocks.note: money in notes and coins, said out loud

explanation.surface: Someone stashing money out of sight of an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store of valuables or supplies, so as a noun it is a hiding place or hoard.

clue.text: Hebrew sad about loaves baked for sabbath

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and moved into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A melancholy Hebrew thinking about the bread prepared for the sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: Shewbread is the biblical bread set out in the Temple, renewed each sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: Shewbread was the twelve consecrated loaves placed before God in the Jewish Temple and replaced every sabbath, as described in Leviticus.

clue.text: Youngster taking male out

indicators.note: out says the following letter is removed from the word it sits in

blocks.note: taking a small portion to try it
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A young person who is ignoring the boys or getting a man out of the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Sampling with its M dropped leaves the answer; youngster is a young tree here, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, and figuratively a young person, so it is a youngster in both plant and human terms.

clue.text: Unusual compass found under edges of seat

indicators.note: edges are the two outermost letters of the following word
in a down clue, a piece found under another is written below it, so it comes second

blocks.note: the outside letters of seat
compass in the sense of scope or extent

explanation.surface: An odd discovery: a compass tucked beneath the edge of a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange is out of the ordinary, which is the plain sense of unusual.

clue.text: Dish of tomato sauce with half of salt omitted

indicators.note: omitted means those letters are left out of the longer word

blocks.note: passata is sieved tomato sauce
the first half of salt

explanation.surface: A recipe note: tomato sauce made with less salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian food served as a meal, typically as a plate of noodles or shapes, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Gelatine is in drinking vessel

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a glass is a vessel to drink from

explanation.surface: A wobbly jelly set in a tumbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but it is simply its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a pure gelatine made from fish swim bladders, used for clarifying beer and wine.

clue.text: Look for bird

blocks.note: first meaning: a quick glance
second meaning: a male goose

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like hunting for a bird, but the two words are separate meanings joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a gander is a glance at something, and the same word names the male of the goose.

clue.text: Dandruff in animal's hair occurring twice

indicators.note: occurring twice tells you to write the piece down two times in a row

blocks.note: the hair coat of an animal
the same piece again

explanation.surface: A vet notices flakes of scurf caught twice in a pet's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Furfur is a rare medical term for scaly flakes of skin on the scalp, i.e. scurf.

clue.text: Letter given to speaker's investigator in government department

indicators.note: given to means the first piece is placed in front of the next one
a speaker says words aloud, so the next word goes by its sound

blocks.note: the name of the letter X spelt out
someone who checks things, said out loud

explanation.surface: A government inspector being handed a letter by a parliamentary speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter here is the alphabet letter X, written as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government department responsible for public revenue, headed by the Chancellor.

clue.text: Relative embracing sources of child's immunisation for young member of the family

indicators.note: sources are where things begin, so the first letters of the next two words
embracing means wrapping arms around, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: a son is a family relative
the first letters of child's and immunisation

explanation.surface: A family member getting a child vaccinated.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a descendant or heir, typically a younger member of a notable family.

clue.text: Foreign weed given to British fool

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and changed, so the letters are rearranged
given to means the next piece is attached after the first

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Some imported cannabis handed to a silly Brit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is slang for a socially awkward, boring or stupid person, a nerd or a dope.

clue.text: Enthusiast to hang elaborate ornament

indicators.note: to here means joined on, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: a fan is an enthusiastic supporter
to dangle is to hang loosely

explanation.surface: A keen collector wanting to hang up a fancy decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Fandangle is an old word for a fantastic or showy trinket, a piece of gaudy decoration.

clue.text: Performer died in front of a tipsy nurse

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before what follows
tipsy means unsteady with drink, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for died
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene: someone dies in front of a nurse who has been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, so he is a stage performer.

clue.text: Childcare provider learnt to accept charge's third animal

indicators.note: third picks the letter in third place of the word before it
to accept means to take something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a nanny looks after children
got in the sense of understood or picked up
the third letter of charge

explanation.surface: A nanny who has learned to welcome her young charge's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like the child in the nanny's care, but only its third letter is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny goat is a female goat, which is a farm animal.

clue.text: Dead skin points to burn

indicators.note: to means joined on, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
to char is to scorch

explanation.surface: A doctor pointing to the dead skin around a burn.
explanation.definitionFit: An eschar is the dry scab of dead tissue that forms over a burn or wound.

clue.text: Colonel slipped then fell over

indicators.note: then puts the second piece straight after the first

blocks.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel
lapsed in the sense of slipped or fell away

explanation.surface: A colonel lost his footing and toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: Collapsing is falling down suddenly, as a person or structure that gives way.

clue.text: Cook made a new fillet

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A chef has prepared a new cut of fish or meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Fillet suggests a cut of meat; here it is a band worn round the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a poetic word for a garland or headband, and a fillet is also a ribbon worn round the hair.

clue.text: Confused smuggler carrying diamonds deserted at end of road

indicators.note: a carrier holds its load inside, so the following pieces sit within the first
the end of a word is its final letter
at here places the last piece after everything else

blocks.note: a mule is a drug smuggler who carries goods across borders
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
D is the abbreviation for deserted
the last letter of road

explanation.surface: A drug mule carrying stolen gems has fled and is lost at the end of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled describes a mind that is in a state of mental disorder and unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Fabric close to crease in sail is damaged

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
damaged means broken up, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the final letter of crease
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor notices fabric failing near a crease in a torn sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a thin twilled cotton or linen cloth used for linings, named after the region it came from.

clue.text: Shift featuring English seamstresses' handiwork

indicators.note: featuring means including, so the second piece is placed inside the first

blocks.note: a swing is a change or shift, as in a swing of opinion
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A work shift including English seamstresses at their craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing is the work of stitching cloth with needle and thread, the job a seamstress does.

clue.text: Direct soldiers next to arms base into annexes

indicators.note: the base of a down word is its bottom, final letter
next to places the two pieces side by side
into puts the earlier pieces inside the word that follows

blocks.note: to annex is to add on
RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps
the last letter of arms

explanation.surface: Orders for troops to be posted beside the armoury and into outbuildings.
explanation.walkthrough: Annexes looks like extra buildings but is the verb meaning adds.
explanation.definitionFit: To address something is to direct it, as a letter is addressed or a remark directed at someone.

clue.text: Get home after boat is damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
after puts the first piece behind the one that follows it

blocks.note: taken as written
in means at home

explanation.surface: Instructions to head home once the boat has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or come by it, the same as to get it.

clue.text: Tree to twist over width of type of recess in wall

indicators.note: to means joined on, so the pieces are written one after another

blocks.note: the bay is a laurel tree
to wind is to twist or coil
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
W is the abbreviation for width

explanation.surface: A tree bending across the width of an alcove in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay window projects outward from a wall to form a recess inside the room.

clue.text: Constituents of nitre surprisingly chemically inactive

indicators.note: constituents are the component parts, which are to be taken apart and reused
surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, here an unexpected order of letters

blocks.note: taken as written; nitre is potassium nitrate

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: saltpetre's ingredients turn out not to react.
explanation.definitionFit: An inert substance does not readily take part in chemical reactions, like the noble gases.

clue.text: Pungent plant without European identity

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed from the word before

blocks.note: acer is the maple genus
E is the abbreviation for European
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A smelly plant lacking any European character.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, bitter smell or taste that stings the nose and throat.

clue.text: King replacing fellow in fake government

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another in the word

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
F is the abbreviation for fellow
to feign is to fake or pretend

explanation.surface: A king steps in to replace a man in a sham administration.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the period of rule by a monarch, so it is a form of sovereign rule over a state.

clue.text: Building material in publicity given award

indicators.note: given means handed on, so the second piece is added after the first

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement
the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a UK honour

explanation.surface: A building supplier wins an award for its advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried brick made of clay and straw, used for houses in dry climates.

clue.text: Leader of lions died during Daniel's unorthodox convincing victory

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so this takes the opening letter
during means within a span, so these pieces sit inside the next
unorthodox means not following convention, so the letters break their usual order

blocks.note: the first letter of lions
D is the abbreviation for died
taken as written

explanation.surface: Daniel in the lions' den, where the chief lion died: a story of an unusual triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Daniel in the lions' den from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an election won by an overwhelming margin, hence a decisive victory.

clue.text: New date not written in series of symbols

indicators.note: new means made over, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A new appointment that hasn't been put down in the diary.
explanation.definitionFit: Notated music or speech is recorded in a system of signs, such as staff notation.

clue.text: Handsome youth is following American college fellow

indicators.note: following places the first piece after those that come next

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good-looking young man trails after a US academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth, so the name stands for any very attractive young man.
